Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
Adult male with 3-day history of frequent watery diarrhea and intermittent left lower abdominal cramps, likely acute gastroenteritis; advised conservative management and follow-up if no improvement.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Watery diarrhea 6–7×/day for 3 days, with intermittent cramp-like pain in left lower abdomen.  
• Associated symptoms: Initial episode of vomiting (now resolved), subjective fever at onset, weakness/shakiness, loss of appetite but tolerating fluids.  
• Pertinent negatives: No blood in stool or vomit; no current fever; no night sweats.  
• Past medical history: Asthma (well controlled).  
• Medications: Asthma inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented; no other medications.  
• Allergies: Not discussed.  
• Social history: Non-smoker, does not drink alcohol; lives with wife and two children; accountant; ate Chinese takeaway 4 days ago (possible trigger); one child had transient vomiting only.

Examination:
• Not performed (telephone/virtual consult).  
• Vitals: Not provided.

Impression:
• Acute gastroenteritis (likely viral; bacterial cause less likely but considered).

Plan:
• Conservative care: Maintain hydration; OTC oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte).  
• Symptomatic relief: Paracetamol 1 g (two 500 mg tablets) up to 4 ×/day as needed for fever or discomfort.  
• Rest/work: Advise 2–3 days off work to recover.  
• Red-flag/return advice: If symptoms persist beyond 3–4 days, worsen, or blood appears in stool/vomit, re-evaluation required; may obtain stool sample for culture at that time.  
• Follow-up: Contact clinic in 3–4 days if no improvement or sooner if concerned.

Quality checks:

● Missing expected elements: Allergies, complete medication list with doses, recent vitals, physical examination findings.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal background noise; no significant inaudible sections.
